domain_context: This scenario reasons over legal case data to (i) match new cases to prior cases that share the same offense, (ii) propagate recommended citations through an existing citation graph, and (iii) surface as relevant only those recommended precedents whose convictions were upheld on appeal. The data sources are: (1) case records with fields (id, name, offense, punishment, decision, convicted), (2) citation edges between cases, and (3) new cases with fields (id, name, offense). The output is the set of relevant convicted precedents per new case.

predicate_verbalization.cases: Existing case arg0 has name arg1, offense arg2, punishment arg3, decision arg4, and convicted flag arg5.
predicate_verbalization.newcase: New case arg0 has name arg1 and offense arg2.
predicate_verbalization.mayCite: New case arg0 may cite case arg1 because they involve the same offense.
predicate_verbalization.shouldCite: New case arg0 should cite case arg1, either directly or through transitive citation.
predicate_verbalization.relevantCase: For new case arg0, case arg1 is a relevant precedent with name arg2 whose conviction was upheld.
